molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.activity_type_context: Sport-related concussion (SRC) in collegiate athletes and its impact on Return-to-Sport (RTS) duration, involving axonal damage and tau dysregulation.
molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.mechanism_description: Sport-related concussion (SRC) involves complex neurobiological effects. Total tau and Neurofilament light chain protein (Nf-L) are microtubule-associated proteins released from neurons, indicating neuronal injury and axonal damage. Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) is released from astrocytes, indicating astrocytic injury. These biomarkers serve as objective measures of injury severity and neuronal recovery. Short-term spikes in total tau may alter tau regulation mechanisms, potentially leading to dysregulation and hyperphosphorylation.

dose_intensity_and_specificity.dose_comparison_summary: The study primarily compared plasma biomarker concentrations in collegiate athletes based on their Return-to-Sport (RTS) duration (<14 days vs. >=14 days), effectively differentiating recovery durations/severities. Additionally, higher Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (GFAP) levels were linked to Sport-Related Concussions (SRCs) with Loss of Consciousness (LOC) and more severe injury in other mTBI studies. Neurofilament light chain protein (Nf-L) concentrations were found to be elevated in military personnel with repetitive Traumatic Brain Injuries (TBIs) compared to those with fewer TBIs.
dose_intensity_and_specificity.specificity_finding: Higher total tau concentrations and lower GFAP levels were specifically associated with return-to-sport decisions, effectively differentiating collegiate athletes based on their recovery time after SRC, with total tau at symptom resolution showing acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.75). However, a combined panel of Nf-L, GFAP, and total tau was generally poor at distinguishing RTS groups (AUC < 0.7) and often added little prognostic ability beyond total tau individually. Nf-L showed limited sensitivity in milder SRC cases and did not significantly discriminate RTS duration in the collegiate cohort, with its utility potentially increasing with more severe or repetitive concussions, as observed in professional athletes or military personnel with multiple TBIs.

clinical_implication_and_population.target_population: NCAA male and female collegiate athletes (mean age 18.9 years, range 17-23 years; predominantly men 76.4%, White 64.6%) who have sustained a sport-related concussion (SRC). Findings may also be applicable to professional athletes and military personnel with TBIs.
clinical_implication_and_population.health_implication: The study identifies objective prognostic indicators to help inform clinical decisions for Return-to-Sport (RTS) after Sport-Related Concussion (SRC). By discriminating RTS duration (less than 14 days vs. 14 days or more) and identifying athletes at risk of prolonged recovery, it aims to improve athlete health and safety. This can reduce the risk of subsequent concussions and mitigate associated long-term negative neurological consequences such as chronic symptoms, functional impairments, and potential neurodegenerative disease, by providing an objective measure for ensuring neuronal recovery before RTS.
clinical_implication_and_population.risk_classification: This research offers both diagnostic and prognostic utility for predicting Return-to-Sport (RTS) duration after Sport-Related Concussion (SRC). It helps identify athletes at risk of prolonged recovery (protracted RTS), thereby highlighting a heightened risk for adverse long-term neurological health outcomes if not appropriately managed, and can inform clinical decisions for a safe return to sport.

biomarker_reliability_and_future_focus.reliability_assessment: Biomarker measurements were performed using ultrasensitive single molecule array (SIMOA) technology, offering significantly higher sensitivity (100-1000 times) than ELISA methods. Assays adhered to standard operating procedures, with samples analyzed in duplicate, and reruns or exclusion if coefficients of variance (CV) exceeded 20% (mean CVs: total tau 7.92%, Nf-L 4.59%, GFAP 3.07%). Total tau at symptom resolution showed fair to acceptable discrimination power for RTS duration (AUC = 0.75). However, a combined panel of Nf-L, GFAP, and total tau was poor at distinguishing RTS groups (AUC < 0.7). Nf-L was not significantly associated with RTS duration in this cohort and is believed to have limited sensitivity in milder SRC cases. GFAP findings were counterintuitive compared to previous mTBI studies, possibly due to varying injury severity or blood sampling timing. UCH-L1 was deemed unreliable due to many samples being below detection limits or having high CVs.
recommended_alternatives: Further research is needed to improve our ability to determine recovery following an SRC.
